subject: Priv toolchain convergence & gate sprint — CI gating and evidence

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Priv toolchain convergence & gate sprint — CI gating and evidence

Hi Jordan, Karthik, Kim —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Per our call, I attached a short proposal that consolidates the Terraform modules, Helm charts, and the Ansible bootstrap flow we plan to deliver for your private VPC/on-prem rollout. High-level goals:

- Reduce duplicate module surface between edge and core stacks so we can certify one set of artifacts for evidence collection.
- Put a CI gating layer in front of Helm/TF/Ansible merges that produces certified artifacts and SBOMs.
- Define a minimal audit bundle (logs, manifest, signed artifacts) for your security review.

Ask: can you confirm the list of non-negotiable evidence items from ACME security? I sketched a proposed list in the attached PDF (redwood-priv-toolchain-proposal-v1.pdf).

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) ACME to confirm mandatory evidence items (security@acme-telecom.com) by 2026-11-12.
2) Our infra team (Karthik/Kim/ Priyom) to produce a CI gating checklist and sample pipeline within 7 business days.
3) Schedule a 60-minute architecture review with ACME security + infra engineers week of 2026-11-16.

Attachments: redwood-priv-toolchain-proposal-v1.pdf

Neha

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priv toolchain convergence & gate sprint — CI gating and evidence

Thanks, Neha —

We reviewed the proposal with our security folks. High level this looks promising but two immediate asks from ACME Security:

1) A machine-verifiable way to produce an evidence bundle for a given release tag (manifest + signed artifacts + provenance). They want a scriptable output we can pull into our compliance platform.
2) A clear separation between customer-managed secrets and any CI artifacts — we cannot accept any pipeline step that requires storing customer secrets in Redwood-managed storage.

I've attached our requirements doc (acme-priv-requirements.pdf) for reference.

Can your team confirm whether the CI gating flow will:
- produce SBOMs and signed Helm/Terraform artifacts?
- emit artifact provenance (e.g., source commit, builder image digest, time, and signer)?

If yes, we can target the week of 11/16 for the architecture review and share two of our engineers. Otherwise, we'll need more details before scheduling.

Jordan Miles
Head of Infrastructure — Acme Telecom
jordan.miles@acme-telecom.com

Subject: Re: Priv toolchain convergence & gate sprint — CI gating and evidence

Jordan / team —

Quick technical notes from our infra side after we read the ACME requirements:

- SBOMs: We can generate SBOMs for container images and packaged charts using the same pipeline that builds and signs artifacts. We'll use syft/grype-compatible formats so ACME can ingest them.

- Signed artifacts: We propose signing Helm charts and TF modules with sigstore (cosign) tied to a Redwood KMS key that can produce attestations. For customer-side signing, we can support an optional step where the customer signs the artifact before accept stage. That satisfies the "customer-managed signing" ask.

- Secrets separation: We will ensure the pipeline steps that need customer secrets run inside a job that mounts only customer-managed KMS credentials (via your KMS connector). Redwood will not persist those secrets in our datastore.

- Provenance: The pipeline will emit a provenance.json with source repo commit, builder image digest, pipeline run id, and cosign attestation digest. We'll add a small shell helper (emit-provenance.sh) that ACME can call to fetch and validate the bundle for any release tag.

Open decisions for the architecture review:
1) Do we default to Redwood-managed signing (cosign) or require customer signing for production artifacts? We recommend default-managed with opt-in customer signing.
2) Do we include a canonical SBOM publish step to the shared compliance bucket (read-only for ACME) or provide a pull endpoint?

I'll prepare a short demo pipeline in our staging project next week. Kim / Priyom — can you review the checklist items and add CI gating job names so Jordan's team can map to their compliance controls?

-karthik

Thanks everyone — quick summary and concrete items before the review next week: 

Summary:
- We can produce SBOMs, cosign-signed artifacts, and a provenance.json file per release tag.
- We will implement a gated CI pipeline that produces an audit bundle for each promoted artifact. 
- Customer-managed signing is supported as an opt-in; default is Redwood-managed signing with attestations.

Action items (owners + target dates):
1) ACME Security (security@acme-telecom.com) — confirm final required evidence items or mark any items as negotiable by 2026-11-23. (Jordan)
2) Karthik — produce a working pipeline demo (staging) that emits signed artifacts + provenance by 2026-11-18. (karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com)
3) Kimberly — publish CI gating checklist (ci-gating-checklist.xlsx) and map each job to ACME control ids (HS-23456) by 2026-11-19. (kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com)
4) Priyom — prepare an internal runbook for the canary rollout in your on-prem environment (include rollback steps) by 2026-11-20. (priyom.das@redwoodinference.com)
5) Neha — schedule the 60-minute architecture review for 2026-11-17 10:00 PT and send calendar invite.

I've attached the checklist and re-attached the proposal for visibility. We'll go through the demo pipeline and decide on signing defaults during the review.

Attachments: ci-gating-checklist.xlsx, redwood-priv-toolchain-proposal-v1.pdf
